si-66mW.title: Landscape: wide east-west valley between mountains
si-66mW.summary: In the southeast: a wide valley running east to west, with mountains to the north and south.

si-9Pxm.title: Bollard: white, black top, bright red front
si-9Pxm.summary: White bollard with a black top, a bright red front reflector and a white back reflector. Austria's is the same shape but darker red in front and black or grey behind. Montenegro is very similar.

differs.how: Austrian front reflector is dark red, back black or grey

si-9zaA.title: House numbers: red with white text
si-9zaA.summary: House numbers are typically red with white text. Czech house numbers are often red too.

si-AOGZ.title: Shed: open hayrack of thin wooden beams
si-AOGZ.summary: A shed called a kozolec, built from thin wooden beams with visible gaps between them, is very typical here.

si-CUtN.title: Km marker: yellow road-number box, black line
si-CUtN.summary: Kilometre markers show the road number in a yellow rectangle at top left, a second number beside it, a black line across, and the distance below.

differs.how: Austrian markers are blue with a white number

si-Dzth.title: Chevron: red arrows on white
si-Dzth.summary: Chevrons usually have red arrows on a white background. A rarer version has a black arrow on white.

differs.how: Austrian chevrons are white on red or red on yellow

si-HIaX.title: Street sign: city emblem, blue shield
si-HIaX.summary: In one city the street signs show its emblem: a blue shield with three yellow stars.

si-Jptp.title: Guardrail: A-type with rounded edges
si-Jptp.summary: Standard A-type guardrail with rounded edges, as in most of Europe. Useful against Croatia, whose B-type guardrail has square edges.

differs.how: Croatian B-type guardrail has square edges

si-KjFQ.title: Google car: black Gen 4 car
si-KjFQ.summary: A black Gen 4 car. Many European countries also have a black car, so it does not narrow things down much.

si-LRnZ.title: Landscape: flat farmland, no mountains
si-LRnZ.summary: In the east: flat or gently rolling farmland with no mountains or tall hills in view.

si-LTMm.title: Sign: yellow direction sign, black border
si-LTMm.summary: Yellow direction signs with a black border. Croatia, North Macedonia, Serbia and Montenegro look similar, while Austria's are white with a blue outline.

differs.how: Austrian signs are white with a blue outline

si-Pi36.title: Language: Č Š Ž letters, no Ć or Đ
si-Pi36.summary: A Slavic language with the letters Č, Š and Ž, closely related to Croatian, Serbian and Montenegrin. Croatian also uses Ć and Đ, which are missing here.

differs.how: Croatian also has the letters Ć and Đ

si-c5sf.title: Landscape: hilly and forested
si-c5sf.summary: Mostly hilly and forested with some farmland. Exceptions are covered in the region clues.

si-d0cG.title: Street sign: white metal-framed or red on walls
si-d0cG.summary: Street signs are most often white with a metal border on posts, or red and fixed to house walls. Most street names contain the word "ulica".

differs.how: Czech red wall signs lack the word "ulica"

si-dqcC.title: Street sign: blue-green shield with black crest
si-dqcC.summary: In one mining town the signs show the city coat of arms: a blue and green shield with a black crest.

si-hUzj.title: Houses: alpine style, dark wood, half-hip roof
si-hUzj.summary: Alpine-style houses with light walls, dark wooden details and fairly steep roofs. The most common roof shape is the half-hip roof.

si-lm-2981.title: Sign: white/silver border, no blue corners
si-lm-2981.summary: Italy, Romania, Serbia and Slovenia look about the same here. Romania has no white or silver border, and Italy shows blue corners outside the white edge.

differs.how: Romanian version has no white or silver border
Italian version shows blue corners outside the white edge

si-lm-783121.title: Language: šola, ulica, lj and nj
si-lm-783121.summary: Slovene has Č, Š, Ž but not Ć or Đ. "Šola" (school) is written škola in Croatian, "ulica" means street, and lj or nj combos mark a South Slavic language, not Czech or Slovak.

differs.how: Croatian also has Ć and Đ, and writes škola

si-mOHj.title: Road lines: long dashes on the outer edge
si-mOHj.summary: Roads commonly have long dashed lines along the outer edge. Neighbouring countries rarely use dashed outside lines.

si-oVxl.title: Coverage: small roads deep in forest
si-oVxl.summary: A big share of the coverage is on small roads deep inside forest.

si-t0v8.title: Sign: Italian bilingual signs
si-t0v8.summary: Signs in Italian as well as the local language appear in the westernmost region.

si-t32B.title: Sign: pedestrian, 5 stripes
si-t32B.summary: Pedestrian crossing sign with five stripes and a simply drawn person with no belt.

differs.how: Austrian sign has two dotted lines

si-ta6V.title: Landscape: tall alpine peaks in the northwest
si-ta6V.summary: The tallest mountains are in the northwestern alpine region.

si-w1wH.title: Google car: white Gen 4 car (rare)
si-w1wH.summary: A white Gen 4 car appears rarely. Other European countries have it too.

si-wTix.title: Landscape: white cliffs, bushes, vineyards
si-wTix.summary: Near the coast: white cliffs with bushy vegetation, vineyards and Mediterranean-style buildings, like the rest of the Adriatic coast.

si-y26n.title: House numbers: green instead of red
si-y26n.summary: In the capital, house numbers are usually green rather than the normal red. Street signs there are sometimes green too.
